object_context: First constructive-continuum atom for issue #87: upgrade regulator/effective-action ultraviolet control for pure four-dimensional Yang–Mills on compact spacetime to cutoff-uniform control of renormalized gauge-invariant observable expectations, strong enough to support an Osterwalder–Schrader-positive, non-trivial continuum Schwinger-function limit before the separate uniform mass-gap and infinite-volume obligations are attacked.

the target theory is pure non-Abelian Yang–Mills for an arbitrary compact simple gauge group, not a Higgs-assisted or matter-coupled theory

continuum existence requires convergence of gauge-invariant observables or Schwinger functions, not merely bounded partition functions or effective actions
local gauge-invariant fields require renormalization/operator mixing while Wilson loops are gauge invariant but nonlocal

cross_domain_analogies.source_situation: A program can be proved to terminate or keep a global invariant while still providing no guarantee that instrumented internal outputs, traces, or probes are stable or semantically correct; adding instrumentation makes the observed interface a first-class object with its own contracts.
common_abstraction: global unmarked stability does not imply stability of marked observables
the observable interface must be transported through every transformation step
correctness of the hidden state evolution and correctness of exposed outputs are distinct obligations
source_to_target_mapping: program global invariant/termination -> partition-function or effective-action ultraviolet stability
observable interface contract -> cutoff-uniform renormalized correlation-function contract
shared_constraints: each transformation can alter how marked information is represented
global stability can coexist with uncontrolled marked outputs
the marked quantity needs an explicit transport law and regression test at every scale
disanalogies: software instrumentation is finite/combinatorial whereas gauge-field observables have ultraviolet singularities and operator mixing
an RG transformation integrates random degrees of freedom rather than preserving deterministic program semantics
cross_domain_analogies.proposed_principle: Treat the observable insertion as part of the RG state rather than attempting to infer observable convergence from an unmarked stability theorem.
cross_domain_analogies.validation_obligation: Before proposing a continuum theorem, exhibit an exact finite-cutoff marked-observable transformation identity for a gauge-invariant test observable, identify its counterterm/mixing closure, and falsify the chosen marked norm on the first scale where uniformity could fail.
cross_domain_analogies.provenance_note: Structural analogy used only to prioritize an observable-marked calibration step; it supplies no Yang–Mills theorem authority.

analogy_scan_notes: Scanned constructive scalar QFT, lattice gauge RG, stochastic gauge-orbit renormalization, Higgs scaling limits, statistical-mechanical source insertions, control/instrumentation, and software verification.
